newsitem.title: FINLAND: UPM-KYMMENE TO HIKE FINE PAPER PRICES.
newsitem.headline: UPM-KYMMENE TO HIKE FINE PAPER PRICES.

text.p: Finnish forestry group UPM-Kymmene said on Wednesday it would raise fine paper prices by 8-12 percent on September 1.
"UPM-Kymmene fine paper division has decided to increase their fine paper prices by 8-12 percent, depending on the market and product, on 1st September 1997," the company said in a statement.
The company said woodfree paper demand in the second-quarter had outperformed new production capacity in Europe and kept orderbooks at an average of three weeks.
"This is still a healthy level considering we are in the middle of the summer season," it said. Overseas demand had also been stronger than assumed, it added.
"The prospects that this healthy demand will continue during autumn and next year are good," the company said.
Wood-free shipments from European mills had grown considerably -- coated wood-free deliveries were up more than 16 percent in H1 and uncoated by more than six percent.

However, UPM said profitability had come under pressure in the early months of the year, as previous price rises in wood free in autumn 1996 and spring 1997 had not compensated "for the current development on the raw material side".
But a company spokesman said UPM's fine paper arm had been profitable and would remain so after the latest price increase.
